summary: Collection window frames may carry sync (StreamSync): this host's replication, explicit when level, so a stream can say a host is behind; clients first, no daemon sends it yet

replay.detail: No claim replay or recovery behavior changes.

schema.detail: No tables, indexes, triggers, schema-version changes or data rewrites. client-v0.schema.json gains StreamSync and an optional sync on the snapshot and changes kinds of CollectionFrame; the generated Rust, TypeScript and Swift clients gain it.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rules or digest changes; no coordinated member upgrade required.

compatibility.detail: Additive and optional on two frame kinds. Clients first: this release only teaches clients to read sync; no daemon sends it until a later release (the daemon change), so a new client on any daemon sees it absent, which means unknown, never level, and keeps reading a page's sync. Older clients ignore the field: the Rust client reads frames by named field and the TypeScript transport parses frames without validating them. External Swift users: a synthesized Codable ignores undeclared keys, but a custom init(from:) or strict decoding of theirs may reject sync on frames once a daemon sends it; no app in this repository uses the Swift package, and its decoder control is written and has not been run (no Swift toolchain on the build host or in CI). Rust source compatibility: st3_client::CollectionEvent::Snapshot and ::Changes gain a sync field, so outside code that matches those variants without `..` must add it (every match in this repository already does).

downtime.detail: No startup work or expected interruption; the daemon is unchanged.

manual.detail: No operator actions, client re-pairing or configuration changes required.

recovery.detail: No persistent state changes or swap-back restrictions.
